common_name: Northern Lights Azalea (Original Cold-Hardy Deciduous Seedling Strain)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in light shade or morning sun; Northern Lights is the original 1978 University of Minnesota release from which the whole cold-hardy Northern Lights azalea series was later selected.

directions: Northern Lights is the founding release in the University of Minnesota's cold-hardy Northern Lights azalea series, introduced in 1978 from an F1 hybrid seedling population raised by crossing Rhododendron x kosteranum with the native, fragrant Rhododendron prinophyllum. Because it was distributed as an open-pollinated seedling strain rather than a single clone, individual plants vary somewhat from light to deep pink, but all share the same clusters of fragrant, funnel-shaped flowers that open on bare branches in mid-spring ahead of the emerging deciduous foliage. It grows larger and more vigorously than most of the later, color-selected named cultivars bred from it, forming a broad, rounded deciduous shrub valued for tolerating winter cold well beyond the range of typical evergreen azaleas. Site it in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in light shade or morning sun, and avoid pruning in fall or winter since next year's flower buds are already set on the current season's growth.
